question: Can a model remain continuously plastic in both weights and topology while serving, using exactly function-preserving structural edits and held-out promotion to make growth safe and empirically useful?

key_findings.claim: The proposed edit algebra can insert width, depth, interfaces, loops, and attention capacity without changing the committed function at the moment of insertion.
key_findings.evidence: Refine, widen, input-growth, zero-initialized residual deepening, and re-founding operators are constructed to preserve outputs at insertion; the audit reports exactness in all 36 tested insertions, no failed serves, and post-edit aliveness in all 36 cases, although only 12 of 36 edits produced immediate descent.

key_findings.claim: Held-out promotion makes topology growth governable, but gate design rather than edit exactness is the principal bottleneck.
key_findings.evidence: The system maintains a served incumbent and speculative working model, promoting only on held-out improvement. In the drift audit, naive gating grew in 3/5 seeds but violated stationary regret in 8/8 checks; silencing the gate reduced growth to 1/5 and still produced two breaches, while incumbent-candidate comparison grew in 1/5 and passed 4/5 non-regret checks. Probes could raise cross-entropy from 4.4-8.2 to 10.5-22.8.

key_findings.claim: The strong hypothesis that structural growth automatically tracks task complexity is refuted; benefits appear mainly when capacity is genuinely binding and probes do not damage the candidate.
key_findings.evidence: With adequate capacity, growth did not track complexity. Under starvation, triggered edits reduced held-out error by 35% and 64%, but only 2/5 candidates were accepted because probing injured the others. In capacity-binding staged control, reward-only growth won 3/5 seeds with mean gain 10.8, whereas outside that regime its mean AUC gap was -33.9; the capacity-sufficient registered comparison missed its value criterion in all 5 seeds.

key_findings.claim: A two-horizon probe statistic is more informative about which kind of structure to add than a single short-horizon gain.
key_findings.evidence: Across the registered direction experiments, the slope between short- and longer-horizon probe gains separated additive from compositional targets, whereas single-horizon improvement did not reliably identify the required direction; targeted depth was strongest at compositional orders 4 and 6, winning 3/3 runs at 58% of the parameters, but was mixed at order 2.

key_findings.claim: Long-sequence plasticity and rehearsal, rather than growth alone, produce the clearest continual-learning advantages.
key_findings.evidence: On 40 full-data permuted tasks, the first-pass decline was lower for the growing model in 10/10 seeds, with grown changes from -2.6 to +5.0 points versus +4.9 to +10.8 for fixed controls. A targeted 60-step refresher raised grown exam accuracy from 0.1818 to 0.2153 while the fixed model fell from 0.1718 to 0.1576, and A-to-B-to-A relearning took 2-3 batches versus 20-29. However, strict sequential domain shifts without review caused 552-1362x degradation on old probes.

key_findings.claim: The empirical support is a small-scale feasibility demonstration, not evidence that self-growing models outperform strong large-model alternatives.
key_findings.evidence: The manuscript describes kilobyte-to-tens-of-kilobyte synthetic systems with mostly three- or five-seed ordinal comparisons and no significance testing. On Split-MNIST, the grown model beat fixed and protocol-twin controls in 9/10 seeds but reached 0.580 final accuracy versus a parameter-matched ceiling of 0.754; a fair uncertainty-controlled rerun was essentially tied, 1.8196 versus 1.8195 median score and 3/5 seed wins.

method.core_idea: Treat model structure as a versioned, editable state: make each edit exactly neutral at insertion, adapt the speculative model, and promote it only when an independent held-out gate prefers it to the served incumbent.
method.mechanism: A recursive substrate applies the same learning primitive at multiple scopes and exposes structural operators for refinement, widening, interface growth, residual deepening, re-founding from stored experience, recurrent loops, and growable heads. Instability EMAs and short/long probe gains nominate an edit; a dual-state gate, resource budgets, audit log, and optional replay govern commitment. All parameters remain plastic rather than freezing old modules.
assumptions: A sufficiently representative and repeatedly usable held-out stream exists for promotion without being adaptively overfit.
Structural edits can be parameterized to preserve the incumbent function exactly and numerical implementations respect that construction.
Short probe trajectories predict the value and direction of longer training without materially injuring candidates.
The chosen gate metric captures the operational harms that should block promotion.
Experience storage and review remain affordable as the lifetime and domain count grow.

techniques.role: Initializes added capacity as an exact identity, copy, zero residual, or equivalent refinement so insertion itself cannot change service behavior.
Separates the committed served state from a speculative candidate and promotes only on held-out improvement.
Uses the slope of short- and longer-horizon gains to choose additive versus compositional growth directions.
Tracks disagreement between signed and absolute updates to nominate stressed units for intervention.
Reuses one target/correction primitive across units, modules, and the whole model instead of assigning a separate optimizer to every scale.
Replays stored observations to recover earlier domains and support re-founding operations.

evaluations.setting: 36 structural insertions in registered synthetic audits
evaluations.metric: Exactness, failed serves, edit aliveness, and immediate descent
evaluations.result: 36/36 exact, zero failed serves, 36/36 alive, but only 12/36 immediately descending
evaluations.baseline: Pre-edit incumbent function and post-edit optimization response

evaluations.setting: Capacity-binding staged quadratic control, five seeds
evaluations.metric: Seed wins and mean score gain
evaluations.result: Reward-only growth won 3/5 with mean +10.8; alternating control won 3/5 with mean +1.1

evaluations.setting: Split-MNIST full-data continual learning, ten seeds
evaluations.metric: Pairwise seed wins and final accuracy
evaluations.result: Growing model beat fixed and protocol twin in 9/10 seeds and was no worse in retention in 8/10, but final 0.580 was only 77% of the 0.754 parameter-matched ceiling
evaluations.baseline: Fixed, protocol-twin, and larger parameter-matched models

evaluations.setting: Forty-task full-data permuted sequence, ten seeds
evaluations.result: Growing model had lower decline in 10/10 seeds; grown range -2.6 to +5.0 points versus fixed +4.9 to +10.8
Full substrate scored 0.762 versus HAT 0.599 and ARF 0.746, but disabling growth changed performance by approximately zero
evaluations.baseline: HAT, adaptive random forest, and no-growth substrate ablation

evaluations.result: Growing and fixed transformer controls were essentially tied at 1.8196 versus 1.8195; growth won 3/5

limitations: Author-stated: experiments are small, predominantly synthetic, and use mostly three- or five-seed ordinal comparisons without significance testing.
Author-stated: a broad comparison against larger-from-birth and wider immobilization families remains open.

Author-stated: the fixed-topology lock-in scenario failed to induce its prerequisite, the re-founding trigger was not validated, self-study did not improve outcomes, and one EWC comparison succeeded in only three of four settings.
Author-stated: repeated reuse of held-out evidence can compromise gate honesty, and the language-model example is a factory demonstration rather than end-to-end structural growth.
Reviewer-identified: many gains come from the plastic recursive substrate or rehearsal rather than accepted topology edits, as the INSECTS ablation and adequate-capacity controls show.
Reviewer-identified: parameter-count matching does not equal compute, optimization, or architecture matching, and the strongest Split-MNIST ceiling substantially exceeds the proposed system.
failure_modes: Probe updates can injure an otherwise promising candidate before the promotion comparison.
Repeated adaptive use of one held-out stream can turn the reality gate into another training signal and admit regressions.
A gate blind to delayed or subgroup harms can approve stationary regret even when its scalar metric improves.
Exact insertion ensures only zero immediate functional change; it does not ensure usefulness, descent, or long-term noninterference.
When capacity is already adequate, growth can add cost without tracking complexity or improving outcomes.
Without replay, strict domain shifts can erase old performance by hundreds-fold despite total plasticity and extra capacity.
Noisy instability thresholds can produce frequent false alarms, while conservative incumbent-candidate gates can suppress useful growth.
reusable_insights: Separate edit safety from edit value: prove insertion equivalence, then evaluate the adapted candidate on independent evidence.
Version structural changes like software deployments, with incumbent rollback, budgets, audit trails, and explicit promotion criteria.
Use multiple probe horizons and their slope rather than a single early gain to infer which capacity axis is binding.
Test growth against both an equal-resource fixed model and a larger-from-birth ceiling; beating only the former does not establish an architecture advantage.
Measure how often an edit is exact, alive, descending, promoted, and useful separately; collapsing them hides the true bottleneck.
Treat rehearsal as an independent design axis: growth supplies capacity but does not by itself preserve old-domain learning signal.
open_questions: How can promotion remain statistically valid under many adaptive candidate comparisons and nonstationary streams?
Can probes predict long-run scaling value without training each candidate far enough to consume the savings growth is meant to provide?
Which gate metrics detect delayed, subgroup, calibration, and reward-hacking regressions rather than only aggregate held-out loss?
When should capacity be added, repurposed, merged, or removed, and can the same guarantees cover shrinkage?
Do the edit algebra and total-plasticity policy remain numerically stable in billion-parameter distributed training?
Can an honest large-scale benchmark disentangle benefits from topology growth, ordinary weight plasticity, replay, and extra compute?

competitive_landscape.title: Net2Net: Accelerating Learning via Knowledge Transfer
competitive_landscape.difference: Net2Net introduced function-preserving widening and deepening to transfer a trained network into a larger one. SoftModel extends neutrality to a broader in-service edit algebra and adds speculative adaptation, promotion, rollback, and lifelong governance; its evidence is much smaller-scale than Net2Net-style supervised acceleration.

competitive_landscape.title: Lifelong Learning with Dynamically Expandable Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: DEN expands at task arrivals using selective retraining, duplication, splitting, and timestamps to control drift. SoftModel instead imposes total plasticity and exact insertion plus a held-out service gate, avoiding DEN's reliance on isolating or selectively freezing old capacity.

competitive_landscape.title: Learn to Grow: A Continual Structure Learning Framework for Overcoming Catastrophic Forgetting
competitive_landscape.difference: Learn to Grow separates task-level structure optimization from parameter learning and selects reuse, adaptation, or new capacity across tasks. SoftModel targets one never-frozen in-service lifecycle with local edit exactness and promotion governance rather than explicit task-boundary architecture search.

competitive_landscape.title: GradMax: Growing Neural Networks using Gradient Information
competitive_landscape.difference: GradMax adds neurons without changing the learned function and initializes them through an SVD objective that maximizes gradient magnitude. SoftModel is broader in structural axes and operational gating, while GradMax gives a sharper train-time criterion for making new capacity immediately optimizable.

novelty_assessment: Author claim: the novel unit is not a single growth operator but a governed lifecycle combining total plasticity, a recursive substrate, exact edits, multi-horizon diagnosis, and held-out promotion. Reviewer inference: exact widening/deepening and dynamic expansion are established ideas, so the clearest novelty is their packaging as versioned in-service structural change with explicit reality gates and audits. The paper is unusually candid that strong complexity-tracking growth is refuted and that replay and substrate plasticity explain several wins. Its scientific contribution is therefore a rich systems hypothesis and failure taxonomy with small-scale proofs of feasibility, not persuasive evidence that autonomous topology growth scales or beats strong fixed architectures.
reviewer_notes: The complete manuscript and appendices were read. Quantitative claims were checked at the cited page markers, especially Tables 3 and 5 and Sections 11-14; negative registered outcomes are retained. Competitor titles, identifiers, and mechanisms were verified on primary arXiv records. Author claims and reviewer inferences are explicitly separated in limitations and novelty assessment.
